## [0.0.8] - 2026-11-23

### Changed

- The README and the configuration and Jelly guides now state what the source returns for the owner, in its pages and
  in `probe`: OpenCode's sign-in for the `wisprflow` server, because Wispr Flow has no tool that names the account. The
  returned owner carries no `verified: false` field today, so a consumer reading only the page must not treat it as a
  verified provider identity. The README's known-limits section now states the conformance report's actual
  not-applicable counts (13 checks for `wisprflow.meetings`, 18 for `wisprflow.meetings.list`), and the conformance test
  comment is corrected to the same counts. Documentation and test comment only; no runtime, descriptor or permission
  behaviour changes.

### Known limits

- **Meetings need Cloud Sync.** A meeting recorded while Dictation cloud storage is off never appears, even after you turn it on.
- **Some Wispr Flow data is out of reach.** No tool reads dictation history, the dictionary, snippets, styles, usage stats or Notetaker chat, and no tool takes audio.
- **The tool list depends on the account.** An active HIPAA agreement or an organisation policy can turn Wispr Flow's MCP off, and a tool the plugin has not classified runs at the `access` value you set.
- **The meetings source sees what Wispr Flow's MCP sees.** Wispr Flow's MCP needs Notetaker and MCP access, Cloud Sync, no active HIPAA agreement and no organisation policy that turns MCP off; it answers "Too many requests" when queries come too fast, publishes no number for that limit, and asks you to wait about a minute ([Wispr Flow](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/9551372685-connect-an-mcp-client-to-wispr-flow-remote-mcp-server)). A listing reads `search_meetings` once per page of 200 meetings of each week, from up to a week behind its cursor, to find a meeting that reached Wispr Flow late. Wispr Flow names no account, so the source's owner is unverified (OpenCode's sign-in, not a Wispr Flow identity): its id is the sign-in's credential id and its label is for display only, so after any new sign-in an old cursor is refused with `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`, and a consumer starts again. The owner today carries no `verified: false` field, so a consumer reading only the page cannot see that it is unverified and must not treat the owner as a verified provider identity. On Wispr Flow's free plan, meetings older than 30 days are locked, and Wispr Flow names no plan, so a listing reaches back at most 29 days on every plan, a day inside the lock: one that starts earlier answers a `gap` (`expired`) once and lists from 29 days ago. A minute Wispr Flow caps (more than 1000 meetings) answers a `gap` (`window-truncated`) and the listing moves past it. A meeting that reaches Wispr Flow after the cursor passed its start (processed late, uploaded from a Mac that was offline, or shared later) is listed on a later read, once, while it started at most a week, or 48 meetings (more when they share a start), behind the cursor. A meeting you delete before it is listed is never listed, and one already listed is not withdrawn.
- **The meetings source's test data is invented.** The conformance kit runs on a synthetic Wispr Flow whose answers follow the JSON shape Wispr Flow's live `search_meetings` returned when last checked; their content is made up, not live-verified. Its report is complete: every check that applies ran. The 13 checks that do not apply to `wisprflow.meetings` (18 to `wisprflow.meetings.list`) are listed in the report; only `failed-holds-cursor` carries a reason: every meeting comes whole from a `search_meetings` listing, and a failed call fails the whole read, so no single meeting fails on its own. `event-within-max-bytes` runs on the events source.
- **Attendee contacts are readable at every `access` value.** `get_participant_contacts` is a read, so it is allowed unless you add a rule for it.
- **Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2.** Other

## [0.0.7] - 2026-11-20

### Added

- **List snapshot** `wisprflow.meetings.list` (`output: "list"`). An app can bind it and render meetings without
  knowing Wispr Flow. It is the tools RPC method `events_list` with `{ "source": "wisprflow", "list": "meetings" }`:
  the model tool's schema has no `list`, so an agent sees no list. It calls the existing `search_meetings` read, not a
  second client, over the last 29 days and returns at most 50 meetings, newest first, each an id and a title; a title is
  screened whole and then cut to 200 characters, control characters are stripped, an id appears once, and the answer
  stops short of 64 KiB. It has no cursor. `wisprflow.meetings` stays the events
  source and is not renamed, and no write is declared.

### Changed

- Source contract `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` v0.3.0 (was v0.2.0), a devDependency bundled into `dist/`
  (no runtime dependency). The declaration and the probe answer are unchanged: the plugin sends none of v0.3.0's new
  keys (`facts`, `hints`, `routines`, an actor's `kind`, `sections` or `parts`), which a consumer still on v0.2.0
  refuses. The conformance test names the seven v0.3 checks the source carries nothing for, each with its reason.
- A listing still reads every sign-in as the free plan, because no Wispr Flow tool names the plan: a read that starts
  more than 29 days ago answers `gap: { reason: "expired" }` once and lists from 29 days ago, so a meeting the plan has

## [0.0.6] - 2026-11-18

### Changed

- Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7, 2.3.0, 2.3.1 and 2.3.2. The supported range is unchanged

A meeting you delete before it is listed is never listed, and one already listed is not withdrawn.
- **The meetings source's test data is invented.** The conformance kit runs on a synthetic Wispr Flow whose answers follow the JSON shape Wispr Flow's live `search_meetings` returned when last checked; their content is made up, not live-verified. Its report is complete: the expired-cursor and gap checks run on a cursor older than the 30-day window, and only the check on `failed[]` is not applicable, with its reason in the report: every meeting comes whole from a `search_meetings` listing and a failed call fails the whole read, so no single meeting fails on its own.

- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.

## [0.0.5] - 2026-11-17

### Fixed

- For Memory: a listing no longer loses meetings that Wispr Flow's free plan hides. On the free plan, meetings older than
  30 days are locked until the account upgrades, and Wispr Flow has no tool that names the plan, so a cursor or a
  `since` that fell behind that window skipped those meetings with no sign. Every sign-in is now read as if it showed
  only the last 30 days, with a day's margin: a read that starts more than 29 days ago answers
  `gap: { reason: "expired", since }` on its first page, `since` being where it started, and lists from 29 days ago.
  The cursor carries that line, so the read's later pages carry no gap, however much later they are read, unless the
  read pauses long enough to fall behind the real 30 days. On a paid plan, `events_list` no longer lists meetings older
  than that either (`search_meetings` still reads them).
- For Memory: a week Wispr Flow caps (more than 1000 meetings) is split and read again, so the cap loses nothing. It
  used to stop with `UNAVAILABLE` and the next step "call events_list again with a later since", which skipped history.
  A minute Wispr Flow still caps is now answered as `gap: { reason: "window-truncated", since }` and passed, so the
  cursor always moves on.
- For Memory: a meeting that reaches Wispr Flow after the cursor passed its start (processed late, uploaded from a Mac
  that was offline, or shared later) is now listed, once. Each read also looks up to a week behind the cursor, and the
  cursor carries a short tag of each meeting it already listed or refused there (48, a few more when meetings share a
  start), so a meeting there without a tag is listed and none is listed twice. A cursor of 0.0.4 still reads, and lists
  nothing again. A meeting you delete before it is listed is never listed, and one already listed is not withdrawn.

### Changed

- The source contract is `@we-the-rebel-alliance/source-contract` v0.2.0 (`#v0.2.0`, 88bdc1e), bundled into
  `dist/index.js` as before, so the package still has no runtime dependency. The declaration and `probe`'s answer are
  unchanged, and a page's only new key is `gap`, which contract 1 already has. This release declares and sends none of
  the keys a consumer on 0.1.x refuses (`removals[]`, an owner's `verified: false`, `permission.identityRules`,
  `accounts.server`, `permission.readsIdentity`, a price's `conditions` or `min`, an empty `permission.identity`). The
  owner is OpenCode's sign-in, not a Wispr Flow identity, so it is unverified; a page and `probe` will say so with
  `verified: false` once Memory and jelly are on 0.2.0.
- The conformance report is complete and ok. The kit's expired-cursor and gap checks run on a cursor older than the
  29-day line. Only the check on `failed[]` is declared not applicable (`atomicPages`), with its reason in the
  report, now exact: `events_list` makes no call per meeting, and a failed `search_meetings` call fails the whole read.
  The report names the contract version it ran from.
- Releases use the family's release kit r4.1 (gws `1f452e5`): `npm run conformance` (`bun test ./test/conformance`)
  writes `reports/conformance-report.json`, the release runs it again on the parent in its own job and stops unless the
  report is ok for the version, and the report becomes the Release asset `conformance-report.json`, listed in
  `SHA256SUMS`. `docs/jelly.md` carries jelly's shared rules, word for word.
- CI's concurrency group names the event (`ci-<event>-<ref>`), so a run by hand never replaces a pending push run.
- Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0 (`TESTED_HOSTS`, unchanged); the supported range is
  still `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0`.

### Known limits

- **Meetings need Cloud Sync.** A meeting recorded while Dictation cloud storage is off never appears, even after you turn it on.
- **Some Wispr Flow data is out of reach.** No tool reads dictation history, the dictionary, snippets, styles, usage stats or Notetaker chat,

## [0.0.4] - 2026-11-15

### Changed

- Admits OpenCode 2.3: the supported range is `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0` (`opencode.host` in `package.json` and `SUPPORTED_HOST`).
  The plugin is tested on 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0: `TESTED_HOSTS` in `src/constants.ts` is that list,
  and the host and pack stages install every release in it, so CI now runs OpenCode 2.2.7 and 2.3.0 too. The
  out-of-range example in the docs and tests is now 2.4.0.
- What OpenCode 2.3 changes does not reach this plugin: it runs no subagents and does not subscribe to
  `session.tool.failed` (it listens only for integration, MCP and credential events), and it has no use for the new
  `session.fork` hook. `events_list` hands the tool's signal to Wispr Flow's `search_meetings`, so it already stops
  when the person presses Stop.
- The icon is now Wispr Flow's own mark, Wispr Flow's five-bar symbol, the dark symbol of Wispr Flow's logo kit, in place of the family's drawn mark; `opencode.vendor.mark` is `true`, and the README says Wispr Flow is a trademark of Wispr AI, Inc.

### Known limits

- **Meetings need Cloud Sync.** A meeting recorded while Dictation cloud storage is off never appears, even after you turn it on.
- **Some Wispr Flow data is out of reach.** No tool reads dictation history, the dictionary, snippets, styles, usage stats or Notetaker chat, and no tool takes audio.
- **The tool list depends on the account.** An active HIPAA agreement or an organisation policy can turn Wispr Flow's MCP off, and a tool the plugin has not classified runs at the `access` value you set.
- **The meetings source sees what Wispr Flow's MCP sees.** Wispr Flow's MCP needs Notetaker and MCP access, Cloud Sync, no active HIPAA agreement and no organisation policy that turns MCP off; it answers "Too many requests" when queries come too fast, publishes no number for that limit, and asks you to wait about a minute ([Wispr Flow](https://docs.wisprflow.ai/articles/9551372685-connect-an-mcp-client-to-wispr-flow-remote-mcp-server)). A listing reads `search_meetings` once per page of 200 meetings of each week. Wispr Flow names no account, so the source's owner is unverified (OpenCode's sign-in, not a Wispr Flow identity): its id is the sign-in's credential id and its label is for display only, so after any new sign-in an old cursor is refused with `ACCOUNT_MISMATCH`, and a consumer starts again. A cursor never expires, and Wispr Flow gives no sign of history it no longer serves, so a listing never reports a gap.
- **The meetings source's test data is invented.** The conformance kit runs on a synthetic Wispr Flow whose answers follow the JSON shape Wispr Flow's live `search_meetings` returned when last checked; their content is made up, not live-verified. Its report is incomplete on one check, the expired cursor, because the source never answers `CURSOR_EXPIRED`.
- **Attendee contacts are readable at every `access` value.** `get_participant_contacts` is a read, so it is allowed unless you add a rule for it.
- **Tested on OpenCode 2.2.3, 2.2.4, 2.2.5, 2.2.6, 2.2.7 and 2.3.0.** Other releases inside `>=2.2.3 <2.4.0` start, and status reports them as untested.
- **Jelly.** The `access` setting declares its choices, which a Jelly needs app#1301 to read; an older Jelly turns the declaration down.
- Updates are not automatic for a Git install, and `opencode plugin update` and `opencode plugin check` do not work on one: to move to a newer release, remove the old entry and add the new tag.
